findings.summary: Requirement R2 mandates the definition of a `repo_context.json` schema including protected path patterns, but Open Question Q14 explicitly identifies the schema definition for these paths as a blocking known unknown, creating a dependency cycle for Milestone M1.

evidence.note: R2 requires definition of repo_context.json schema with protected paths
evidence.quote: The Implementation Council subsystem SHALL define and require a typed, versioned repo_context.json schema

evidence.note: Q14 marks the schema for protected paths as a blocking open question
evidence.quote: What is the required schema for repo_context.json protected paths/forbidden paths

findings.summary: Requirement R3 mandates `workspace_context.json` include retention/compaction policies, but Open Question Q16 identifies workspace retention periods and compaction triggers as unresolved, potentially impeding the full schema definition required for Milestone M1.

evidence.note: R3 requires retention/compaction policies in workspace_context.json
evidence.quote: SHALL declare at minimum: ... retention/compaction policies

evidence.note: Q16 asks for max workspace size and retention period
evidence.quote: What is the maximum workspace size and retention period

findings.summary: Sample check R1: Requirement/AT1 specify plan_package_final.json plus an associated structured handoff bundle as the sole canonical planning input, but M1 deliverables only explicitly mention validating/recording plan_package_final.json; the plan does not explicitly state that the structured handoff bundle is validated and persisted as part of intake deliverables/checks.

evidence.note: R1 includes 'plan_package_final.json (plus its associated structured handoff bundle)' as sole canonical planning input
AT1 run (a) includes 'plan_package_final.json plus its structured handoff bundle'
M1-D1 mentions only 'Validated plan_package_final.json accepted and recorded' (no explicit handoff bundle validation/recording deliverable)

findings.summary: Sample check R2: repo_context.json minimum required fields include language (and/or explicit ecosystem metadata) in addition to build-system entrypoints, but milestone/AT2 descriptions do not explicitly require a language field; this may leave the repo_context schema under-specified relative to R2.

evidence.note: R2 minimum fields include 'language/build-system entrypoints'
M1-D2 lists repo root, build entrypoints, validator entrypoints, protected/forbidden paths, branch/commit metadata; does not explicitly mention language metadata
AT2 required-fields parenthetical mirrors M1-D2 and does not explicitly include language metadata

findings.summary: Sample check R3: R3 states workspace_context.json must be required before any workspace-writing stage begins, but the Intake stage tool policy allows workspace_write (noncanonical-only). Unless clarified that workspace writes are forbidden until workspace_context is validated (or that Intake does not write at all), this is a potential ordering/policy mismatch for the sample check.

evidence.note: R3 requires workspace_context.json before any workspace-writing stage begins
Intake restrictions allow workspace_write: 'allow_noncanonical_only'
Intake HITL trigger includes missing workspace_context.json, but policy still indicates workspace_write is permitted in Intake

findings.summary: R1 milestone mapping includes M2 (Work Plan Compilation) but requirement text does not explicitly mandate work plan stage validation of plan_package_final.json acceptance; M2 should validate no semantic drift but R1 is about input acceptance which is purely M1 scope.

evidence.note: R1 text focuses on input acceptance and rejection of non-canonical sources
M1 exit criteria cover input validation and acceptance
M2 validates no semantic deviation but this is scope control not input acceptance
evidence.quote: No semantic deviation from frozen plan entities; validator confirms no new R#/AT#/O#/K# introduced (K1 mitigation).

findings.summary: R2 and R3 both map to M1 and M2 milestones, but the requirement text states these schemas are required 'before any code-generation stage begins' (R2) and 'before any workspace-writing stage begins' (R3). M2 (Work Plan Compilation) does not perform code generation or workspace writing per its deliverables, so M2 mapping appears conservative but not strictly required by the requirement text.

evidence.note: R2 requires repo_context.json before code-generation stage
evidence.quote: SHALL be required before any code-generation stage begins

evidence.note: R3 requires workspace_context.json before workspace-writing stage
evidence.quote: SHALL be required before any workspace-writing stage begins

evidence.note: M2 produces work_plan.json but does not generate code or write workspace canonical artifacts per stage restrictions

findings.summary: AT1 maps to R1 and tests input acceptance/rejection, which is correctly covered by M1 exit criteria. However, the sample check does not verify that M1 exit criteria explicitly test rejection of chat logs and non-canonical artifacts as specified in AT1 procedure, only that plan_package_final.json is accepted.

evidence.note: AT1 procedure requires testing rejection of chat log and non-canonical artifact inputs
evidence.quote: Attempt to initiate an Implementation Council run with inputs: (a) valid plan_package_final.json; (b) chat log reference; (c) unapproved non-canonical artifact as planning input.

evidence.note: M1 exit criteria confirm plan_package_final.json acceptance but do not explicitly enumerate rejection test cases
evidence.quote: All three input artifacts pass schema validation (AT1, AT2, AT3).
